mapping_note: Field names in scripts/roi_math.py are repurposed for this business and the study must state the mapping. 'pursuits_per_year' means GUEST CONTACTS TO THE RESERVATION DESK PER OPERATING SEASON, not per calendar year, because the railway runs April 30 to October 7, 2026 (c16). 'years': 5 therefore means five operating seasons. 'hours_per_pursuit' is the AVERAGE agent hours per contact across the whole contact population, not the hours on an affected contact only. 'cut' is the REALISABLE share of that time, already net of the avoid-backfill test described in the benefit notes, so it is not the theoretical time saved. A fourth scenario key, conservative_breakeven_probe, is NOT a forecast. It holds every conservative assumption fixed and varies only the season contact count, so the code prints the contact volume at which the pilot returns its full five-year cost. It exists to hand the reader the lever rather than an answer.
cost_note: Five-year total cost of ownership, not sticker price, and the ask and the TCO are two different numbers that the study states separately so neither hides the other. THE ASK IS THE YEAR ONE CHEQUE, implementation plus training plus contingency, which lands inside the 25 to 30 thousand dollar envelope the pre-check sized in all three scenarios and at the top of it in the conservative case, because the conservative case pads cost rather than trimming it. THE TCO IS LARGER because it carries four and a half further years of run cost, and the study prints both. WHAT IMPLEMENTATION BUYS, and it is the biggest line as ROI_METHOD says it usually is, the structured multilingual request form with dropdowns and an unvalidated booking reference field, the server-side arrival timestamp write, the work-item queue and the four counters, the timestamped ingest on info@wpyr.com, the out-of-hours greeting and callback capture configuration on the 1-800 line, the single governed source of policy text that fixes the cancellation page carrying no hours while the product pages do, professional human translation of the fixed strings and the acknowledgement templates into Spanish and Japanese, and exhaustive tests on the 24 hour boundary and the Alaska Time conversion. TRAINING AND CHANGE MANAGEMENT IS STATED IN HOURS, NEVER 'INCLUDED', 16 hours of their staff time in year one, 10 for the reservation desk, 4 for the Manager of Reservations and Sales, 2 for whoever administers the phone system, plus a written runbook and two facilitated sessions from us, and a further 4 hours at the start of each subsequent season for seasonal onboarding. RUN COST carries hosting, the telephony line item, monitoring and uptime, an annual re-review of the translated policy strings whenever the policy changes, and our in-season support. THERE IS NO INFERENCE OR TOKEN COST AND NO MODEL REFRESH LINE, because phase one carries no model at all, which is the single largest reason this TCO is small. HUMAN REVIEW IS NOT ADDED AS A RUN COST, because the queue is worked by the reservation agent who handles these contacts today, and that labour is netted inside the benefit lines rather than counted twice. CONTINGENCY IS 20 PERCENT in the conservative and most likely cases and 15 percent in the aggressive case, at the top of the 15 to 20 band, because ROI_METHOD is explicit that most failures come from organisational factors rather than software. PHASE 2 AND THE SELF-SERVICE CANCELLATION DESK ARE NOT PRICED HERE. Both are gated on measured results and neither appears anywhere in this cost stack or this benefit stack.

benefits.benefit: Reservation desk handling time per guest contact, a structured request that arrives complete instead of a voicemail or a free-text email that has to be reconstructed
benefits.basis: ASSUMED, and every input is an assumption because nothing here is published. Conservative case assumes 3,600 guest change, cancellation and question contacts across one operating season, an average of 0.30 agent hours per contact today end to end including the round trip to establish intent, booking reference and departure, a fully loaded seasonal agent cost of $32 an hour, and a realisable 18 percent of that time removed. The only published volume anchor in the file is almost 2,000 train starts a season (c7). No call volume, no email volume, no channel split and no passenger count is published anywhere, so the contact count is an assumption and is the first driver the reader should challenge. The mechanism is grounded in the company's own pages, the Reservation Agent enters bookings and answers the same questions across phone, email and in person (c30), cancelling or altering a booking requires a phone call with no online path (c11), and the office runs Monday to Friday 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM Alaska Time (c10), which is 40 of the 168 hours in a week.
benefits.note: CAPACITY, and it is in the formula only at the share that passes a stated conversion test. THE TEST MET IS AVOID-BACKFILL, not headcount reduction. The desk is seasonally staffed, the company publishes a May 1 to September 30 recruiting season (c35) and listed Reservation Agent openings for Carcross and Whitehorse in 2026 (c32), so a seasonal desk shift is re-decided every spring and hours removed can be realised as a shift not covered without a layoff and without touching the represented onboard workforce (c33). The 18 percent cut is the realisable share, not the theoretical one. THE OTHER USE OF THESE HOURS IS DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED. The same agent is pulled onto the platform for train loading and crossing-guard duty (c30) on days when five ships were listed arriving (c20), so hours returned during a loading window get redeployed rather than banked, which is real and is quarantined out of the formula rather than converted.

benefits.benefit: Repeat published-policy questions answered by the governed policy source at the point of request, instead of by an agent
benefits.basis: ASSUMED. Conservative case assumes an average of 0.10 agent hours per contact spent on repeat published-policy questions, the same $32 fully loaded hourly cost, and 30 percent of that removed by deflection. The defect it fixes is verified rather than inferred, the cancellation page itself states no office hours (c11 scope note), the contact page carries none either (c18), the hours live only on product pages (c10), and the navigation link labelled FAQ points at the travel blog (c34, used as evidence only and never as a headline). A guest asking when they can call to cancel currently has no page that answers it.
benefits.note: CAPACITY, converted on the same AVOID-BACKFILL test and at the same stated realisable share. THIS LINE DOES NOT DOUBLE COUNT THE LINE ABOVE, and the study says so explicitly. The two mechanisms are disjoint. The first shortens a contact the agent still handles. The second removes a contact from the queue entirely. Together they remove about 302 agent hours from an assumed seasonal handling pool of about 1,440 hours in the conservative case, which the reader can check against the driver table. If a reader thinks the two overlap, zeroing this line is the correct test and the conservative case should be re-read with it at zero.

benefits.benefit: Guest escalations and card disputes that begin with an unreachable office inside the 24 hour refund clock
benefits.basis: ASSUMED, with the mechanism verified and the volume invented, and the study labels it that way. Conservative case assumes 40 escalations a season, a blended $220 per escalation covering agent and manager research and response time plus the discretionary goodwill portion, and a 30 percent reduction. The mechanism is the company's own published policy read together, a cancellation up to 24 hours prior gets a refund minus a $10.00 per person penalty and a cancellation within 24 hours forfeits all rights to a refund (c12), the only published route to act is a phone call (c11), and that route runs 40 hours a week (c10). Fares run $155 adult and $77.50 child on the Summit and $289 adult on Bennett (c15), so a forfeited family booking is a large and highly escalation-prone event. NO DISPUTE COUNT IS PUBLISHED AND WE HOLD NO SAMPLE, since zero verbatim customer reviews were obtainable and every review platform returned HTTP 403.
benefits.note: CASH, because an escalation consumes manager time and sometimes a discretionary refund, both of which are real outflows rather than freed capacity. It is the weakest-evidenced line in the stack and it is the second line a skeptical reader should zero out as a test. It is also the smallest contributor in every scenario, which is deliberate. Note what is NOT in this line, a resold seat. Nothing anywhere in this case assumes the railway resells a seat that a newly reachable guest gives back.

qualitative_quarantine: OUT-OF-HOURS CAPTURE ITSELF. Capturing a contact against a server-written arrival time when the office is shut is the whole mechanism of this build, and it carries no separate dollar line. Its value flows through the three quantified lines above and nowhere else. Counting it again as its own benefit would be double counting the same event.

THE FOUR COUNTERS, which are the primary return of this ask and are deliberately outside the formula. Out-of-hours contact volume, arrival time relative to the 24 hour cutoff, language mix and intent mix do not exist today and can't be bought. Phase one produces them as a by-product of the agent doing the job they already do, at zero added workload. Putting a one-time decision value into an annual run-rate line would inflate it five times over, so it is stated in prose and left out of the arithmetic.

REDEPLOYED AGENT HOURS during train loading. c30 says the reservation agent is pulled onto the platform for loading and crossing-guard duty, and c20 lists five ships arriving on a single August day. Hours returned inside a loading window are genuinely useful and they do not reduce a cost, so they are named and not converted.

CHANGE AND ADD REQUESTS captured out of hours that today die against a closed office. Excluded on purpose, because whether a seat exists to sell against a request depends on the sell-out rate by departure, and the trains usually sell out in advance (c14) with no rate published. That is the same unpublished number the resold-seat argument rests on, so it is excluded for the same reason.

RESOLD SEATS AFTER AN EASIER CANCELLATION, excluded entirely and in both directions. Today a guest who can't reach anyone forfeits the fare and the railway keeps it (c12). A build that lets that guest cancel at 9pm Saturday converts a forfeiture into a refund minus $10.00. Whether the resale plus the avoided dispute beats the kept fare depends on their sell-out rate by departure, which they do not publish, so easier cancellation is not unambiguously positive in the short run and this case shows neither side of it.

LEGAL EXPOSURE reduced by a single governed source of policy text. Under Moffatt v. Air Canada the company is responsible for what its own website says regardless of who built it, and the tribunal rejected the separate entity argument (c44). Real, and unquantifiable from outside.

GOODWILL AND CHANNEL STANDING with the cruise shore-excursion desks that sell this product (c13), one of whose parent is a minority partner in the ownership group (c5). No sample of guest sentiment was obtainable, so there is nothing honest to size it with.
benefit_phasing: No day-one full benefit anywhere in this case. Year one is partial and the ramp is stated as a driver rather than described, 25 percent in the conservative case, 30 percent most likely, 40 percent aggressive, which encodes a ninety-day stabilisation on top of a hard calendar constraint that is specific to this company. THE 2026 SEASON CLOSES OCTOBER 7 (c16) AND TODAY IS AUGUST 9. The eight weeks remaining are calendar time and not usable observation time, because build, access to info@wpyr.com and telephony configuration all come out of the same eight weeks, so the honest year-one ramp here is thinner than a normal ninety-day ramp rather than fatter. Whatever is captured before the close is also a SHOULDER SEASON SAMPLE, since Bennett closes September 12 (c17) and the Summit season carries no service on September 26 to 27 and October 1 and 3 to 5 (c16), so a question mix measured in September describes a shoulder period and must be labelled that way before anyone designs 2027 on it. Year two is the first full operating season at run rate. Year three onward compounds only through the counters improving the routing rules and the governed policy text, not through any new capability, because no new capability is priced here. One honest rider on the shape of the curve, the arithmetic treats a year as an operating season while the railway runs roughly five months of the twelve, so benefit lands in a burst each season rather than evenly across the calendar, and a payback month printed by the model is a smoothed figure.

conservative.note: THE CASE TO READ, and it clears its bar without a single resold seat, without any decision-data value in the formula, and with cost padded rather than trimmed. THE BAR, stated plainly so nobody can call it moved afterwards. One, the pilot returns its full five-year cost from labour capacity converted on a named avoid-backfill test plus escalation cash alone. Two, it does that with zero dollars attributed to resold seats, to the four counters, or to any qualitative benefit. Three, the year-one cheque stays inside the 25 to 30 thousand dollar envelope the pre-check sized. All three hold at these drivers, and the code prints the recovery percentage and the payback month rather than this note asserting them. THE SENSITIVITY THE READER MUST SEE, the answer turns on the season contact count and on nothing else nearly as much. The breakeven probe below prints the contact volume at which the case returns exactly its cost, and if their own phone log and inbox come back under that number, the honest conclusion is that this build does not pay on labour and phase two should not be funded. Cost is padded here rather than trimmed, implementation is $2,000 above the most likely figure and run cost is $400 a season above it, so the conservative case is conservative on both sides of the ledger.

aggressive.note: NOBODY SHOULD BUY ON THIS COLUMN AND THE STUDY SAYS SO IN THE TABLE. It assumes 7,000 contacts a season, a $40 fully loaded rate, 30 and 45 percent realisable cuts, 100 escalations at $300 with a 45 percent reduction, a clean build at $18,000, and a 40 percent year-one ramp that would need the system live well before the October 7 close. The recovery multiple this column prints will look very large, and the honest reason is arithmetic rather than performance, the ask is small relative to a seasonal desk's labour pool, so any real saving divides into a small denominator. It is capped where it is because the drivers already remove about a third of the assumed seasonal handling pool, and anything above that would be removing more work than the desk plausibly does. Contingency drops to 15 percent here, the bottom of the permitted band, which is part of why it is the aggressive column.

payback_range: A RANGE, computed in code, never narrated here. The study prints the band running from the conservative payback month to the most likely payback month as produced by scripts/roi_math.py from the drivers above, and it never prints a single hero month. Three riders travel with the band and all three ship. ONE, the conservative end is the one to plan against, and it is the only end that carries no resold seat, no decision-data value and no qualitative benefit. TWO, the arithmetic spreads a season's benefit evenly across twelve months while the railway operates roughly five months a year (c16), so a printed month is a smoothed figure and the benefit really arrives in a burst each season. THREE, the whole band collapses if the season contact count lands under the breakeven probe volume, in which case there is no payback inside the five-season horizon, the honest answer is that this does not pay on labour, and phase two does not get funded. Any payback shorter than six months would imply unusually high volume or a tiny scope, and if the printed conservative figure comes in that fast the right response is to distrust the volume assumption rather than celebrate it.
base_rate_note: THE OUTSIDE VIEW, stated before the inside view and with a wrinkle that cuts against our own pitch. THE BASE RATE IS BAD. MIT's work puts roughly 95 percent of AI pilots at no measurable P&L impact and RAND puts around 80 percent of AI projects as failures, and reference-class forecasting says the correct starting assumption for a proposal like this one is that it joins them. In this specific industry the local reference class is thin as well, only 12 percent of tour, activity and attraction operators actively use AI in their operations, with most still experimenting or not using it at all, from Arival's survey of more than 7,000 operators published October 22, 2024 (c42). Thin adoption means there is no local proof this works and no local proof it does not, which is an argument for buying measurement before buying a model, not an argument that everyone else is behind. THE HONEST WRINKLE, AND IT CHANGES HOW THE BASE RATE APPLIES RATHER THAN EXEMPTING US FROM IT. Phase one contains no artificial intelligence at all. It is a form, a server-written timestamp, an inbox ingest, a phone greeting and a governed content file. The failure modes that generate the MIT and RAND numbers are mostly model-shaped, no evaluation set, no clean data, hallucination on a liability surface, inference cost, an integration nobody assessed, drift after launch, and almost none of them can reach a system with no model in it. What phase one keeps from that base rate is the part that has nothing to do with AI, adoption. A tool the desk works around is dead whether or not it has a model, and that is the risk this build actually carries. WHERE THE AI BASE RATE DOES APPLY IS PHASE TWO, the single-node classifier on inbound free text, and phase two is not funded by this ask. It is gated on counters phase one produces, on an evaluation set built from real 2026 traffic, and on an acceptance bar set before the model is built, which is the specific discipline the failed 95 percent skip. WHY THIS ONE IS DESIGNED TO BE IN THE SMALL SHARE THAT PAYS. It is workflow-embedded rather than bolted beside the workflow, the queue is the same work the reservation agent does today with an arrival time attached (c30). It is adoption-owned by a named person on their side. It is measured, and the measurement instrument is the deliverable rather than a promise about one. Its floor is strictly above the status quo, because the timestamp is a server write and a total failure of anything downstream degrades to today's behaviour plus a timestamp. AND THE PART A VENDOR WOULD NOT SAY, we are recommending they buy an off-the-shelf tourism chat widget at published list pricing of $95 to $295 a month (c48) that we are not paid for, with the warning that under c44 the liability for what it says stays with them. Reference-class evidence we are using is labelled by tier and never used as this company's baseline, the Black Cat Cruises figures are vendor published with 10 hours a month the trustworthy number, the modelled $3,750 never quotable as revenue, and only 10 percent of site visitors leaving an email address, which cuts against capture optimism (c47). Amtrak's ARROW at 3 to 5 percent is a real precedent for a different problem (c43). Chipotle's 12 days to four and 30 percent of scheduling after hours were reported by Fortune in its own voice, and Chipotle is enormous, so the direction transfers and the magnitude does not (c46). None of those is this company's baseline and none is used as one.
value_owner: ALLYSON NANNINI, MANAGER OF RESERVATIONS AND SALES, owns the number. She is on the published leadership directory, she owns the desk this lands on, and she owns the queue and the four counters it produces. Executive sponsor is VICKEY MOY, EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR OF PASSENGER OPERATIONS, who owns the platform-side consequence when agents are pulled onto train loading. Approval sits with BOB BERTO, PRESIDENT, who is also named as a director of the majority partner, so the operating decision and the ownership vote sit with the same person and this does not have to travel to an absentee owner. One item is confirmed with the company before anything ships rather than assumed, about 40 workers voted to join SMART-TD's local chapter on April 8 (c33), Reservation Agents are not among the roles that article names, and absence from a list is not proof of non-representation. THE VARIANCE CHECK, and it has an unusual shape here because there is no baseline to vary against yet. Two weeks before go-live, the desk logs contacts by channel and by hour from its own phone log and inbox, which produces the pre-baseline the whole case is missing. The first 30 days after go-live produce the measured baseline from the counters themselves. Actual versus baseline is then read at 60 days, at 90 days and at season close on the four drivers that move the answer, contacts a season, average handling minutes a contact, deflection rate on published-policy questions, and escalations a season. Every one of those is compared against the driver table in this study, line by line, and the variance is published to Nannini, Moy and Berto whether it is good or bad. Two rules ride with it. The 2026 reading is a shoulder-season sample and is labelled one, because Bennett closes September 12 (c17) and the Summit season carries no service on several late dates (c16), so a September count understates a July peak and may not be annualised without saying so. And if the measured contact count lands under the breakeven probe volume, the correct outcome is that phase two is not funded and this pilot did its job by saying no.
assumptions: EVERY VOLUME DRIVER IN THIS CASE IS AN ASSUMPTION, NOT A FACT. No channel split, no passenger count, no trains-per-day figure, no call or email volume and no year-round versus seasonal headcount split is published anywhere. The 500,000 figure is recruiting copy and the newest count the company publishes itself is 385,000 from 2012, and neither is used as a baseline anywhere in this case.

Guest contacts to the reservation desk per operating season, assumed at 3,600 conservative, 6,000 most likely, 7,000 aggressive. The only published volume anchor in the file is almost 2,000 train starts a season (c7). This is the single driver the answer turns on and their own phone log and info@wpyr.com inbox settle it in an afternoon.

Average agent hours per contact today, end to end including the round trip to establish intent, booking reference and departure, assumed at 0.30 conservative, 0.35 most likely, 0.35 aggressive. No handling-time baseline exists.
Average agent hours per contact spent on repeat published-policy questions, assumed at 0.10 conservative, 0.12 most likely, 0.12 aggressive.

Fully loaded hourly cost of a seasonal reservation agent, assumed at $32 conservative, $36 most likely, $40 aggressive, covering wage, payroll load and seasonal accommodation. No wage figure is published by the company and this is a modelled range, not a measurement.

Realisable share of handling time removed by structured intake, assumed at 18 percent conservative, 25 percent most likely, 30 percent aggressive. This is the realisable share and not the theoretical one, it is already net of the avoid-backfill test.
Realisable share of repeat policy questions deflected by the governed policy source, assumed at 30 percent conservative, 40 percent most likely, 45 percent aggressive.

Escalations and card disputes per season arising from an unreachable office inside the 24 hour clock, assumed at 40 conservative, 70 most likely, 100 aggressive, at a blended $220, $260 and $300 each, reduced 30, 40 and 45 percent. No dispute count is published, no goodwill-refund figure is published, and zero verbatim customer reviews were obtainable because every review platform returned HTTP 403, so we hold no sample of how these guests behave when this happens to them.

Capacity converts to cash on an AVOID-BACKFILL test and on no other test. The desk is seasonally staffed against a published May 1 to September 30 recruiting season (c35) with Reservation Agent openings listed for 2026 (c32), so hours removed can be realised as a seasonal shift not covered, without a layoff and without touching the represented onboard workforce (c33). No defer-hire and no redeploy dollars are claimed anywhere.

The two labour lines are asserted to be disjoint mechanisms, one shortening a handled contact and the other removing a contact from the queue. If a reader disagrees, zeroing the second line is the correct test and the conservative case should be re-read with it at zero.

Implementation assumed at $21,000 conservative, $19,000 most likely, $18,000 aggressive. Training and change management assumed at $3,000, $2,500 and $2,200, covering 16 hours of their staff time in year one and 4 hours per season after, with our materials and facilitation.

Run cost per season assumed at $3,000 conservative, $2,600 most likely, $2,400 aggressive, over 4.5 years. It carries no inference cost, no token cost and no model refresh, because phase one carries no model. Human review is not added as a run cost because the queue is worked by the agent who handles these contacts today, and that labour is netted inside the benefit lines rather than counted twice.
Contingency assumed at 20 percent conservative and most likely, 15 percent aggressive, inside the 15 to 20 band.

Year-one ramp assumed at 25 percent conservative, 30 percent most likely, 40 percent aggressive. The 2026 season closes October 7 (c16) and today is August 9, and build, inbox access and telephony configuration all come out of the same eight weeks, so the year-one ramp here is thinner than a standard ninety-day ramp rather than fatter.

Any 2026 measurement is a shoulder-season sample. Bennett closes September 12 (c17) and the Summit season carries no service on September 26 to 27 and October 1 and 3 to 5 (c16), so a question mix or contact count captured this season describes a shoulder period and may not be annualised without that label attached.

NOT ASSUMED ANYWHERE IN THIS CASE, a resold seat. Today a guest who can't reach anyone inside 24 hours forfeits all rights to a refund and the railway keeps the fare (c12), and a build that lets that guest cancel at 9pm Saturday converts a forfeiture into a refund minus a $10.00 per person penalty. Whether the resale plus the avoided dispute beats the kept fare depends on their sell-out rate by departure, the trains usually sell out in advance (c14) and no rate is published, so easier cancellation is not unambiguously positive in the short run and this case claims neither direction.

NOT ASSUMED ANYWHERE, any benefit from booking validation, booking lookup, a seat release or anything that writes to the ticketing system. That integration is out of phase one and can't be assessed from outside the company, and the booking reference is captured as an unvalidated string.

The observation that the ticketing system returned an unavailable message on 2026-08-09 (c19) is point-in-time, could be transient, is never presented as a standing condition, and carries no weight in any driver in this case.

The absence of a published IT lead on the company directory is an unverified inference about the directory and never a fact about the company. It shapes delivery toward a managed, low-maintenance build and is not used as a benefit driver.
Phase 2 and the self-service change and cancellation desk are NOT priced here, appear in no cost line and in no benefit line, and are gated on the counters this pilot produces.
